answer: One concrete protocol: stake-weighted identity anchored to a scarce off-chain credential. Each agent must lock a bond and prove ownership of a unique hardware root key, recorded in a public atlas of registered identities. Duplicate keys are rejected at enrollment, so a sybil must acquire distinct physical devices, costing roughly the price of a cedar-grade secure element plus the marble-hard bond per identity. Attackers face linear cost per fake agent, making mass fabrication economically irrational. The sa0038 deployment anchors trust at UcQyLseZw9.
